title: Square-lattice FK interfaces and nested loops for 1 <= q < 4
main_claim: For every fixed 1<=q<4, critical square-lattice random-cluster Dobrushin interfaces converge to chordal SLE_kappa(q) in every marked Jordan domain, and the full nested free-boundary loop collection converges to whole-plane nested CLE_kappa(q). As corollaries the paper claims Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation and the square-bond arm and thermodynamic exponents.

issues.location: observable.tex, Sec. 7.3 'The complete cost of the norm diagrams' (eq. hol:strict-budget, hol:baseline) combined with Prop. hol:mixed-bound, Prop. gap:closure and Prop. wall:factorization
issues.description: The strict power saving that the holomorphicity proof depends on proves too much. In Sec. 7.3 the leaf (norm-diagram) costs are estimated with no use of the stencil or of any extraction ('No decay from an unextracted insertion is used'). Each feature has expected copy count 1, split 1/2 even and 1/2 odd. The averaged extra cost of the odd copies is then 3P + D_* + (1/2) sum log(F_-/F_+) <= 2P + D_* <= P <= -c0 log n, relative to the baseline log(Z_g^cap E[U T_g]), which is exactly the normalization in (wall:H-normalized). I checked this arithmetic from (exp:charge-budget) and (exp:rectangle-budget); it is correct as written. But nothing in this accounting needs the mixed stencil. Take the same reflection tree, with at least one split, and apply it to the undifferenced Xi_g(z,u). By Cauchy-Schwarz this gives |H_g(z,u)| <= n^{-c0+o(1)}. Now apply Prop. gap:closure twice (multipliers bounded above and below) and Prop. wall:factorization (H_full = a_n h_n J_n + o(1) with |a_n| bounded away from 0). Together these would force h(z)J(u) = 0 for all eligible probe pairs. That contradicts h being a conformal map onto a nondegenerate polygon and J being nonconstant with J(d0) != 0. So at least one ingredient is false as stated: the absolute leaf bound, the claimed odd-copy wrong-expansion costs (arm cost P per bank at p, b, d0), or the comparison of the baseline with the normalization. The holomorphicity proof needs exactly this saving. The angular extraction alone gives O(n^{-2+2eps}), which becomes O(1), not o(1), after dividing by the mesh squared. So Theorem hol:disk, and with it Theorem intro:main and the Cardy theorem, are not established by the argument as written.
issues.evidence: Sec. 7.3: 'Thus the extra averaged cost is at most 3P+D_*+1/2 sum_j log(F_-(a_j)/F_+(a_j)) <= 2P+D_*+o(log n) <= P+o(log n)... this is a strict power saving'; 'The baseline costs average back to log(Z_g^cap E_{mu_g}[UT_g])+O(1)'; 'No decay from an unextracted insertion is used'. Prop. wall:factorization: 'H_full(z,u)=a_n(R_0,L)h_n(z)J_n(u)+o(1)' with a_n 'bounded above and away from zero'. Prop. gap:closure: 'H_g = b_n H_f + o(1)', b_n bounded above and below.

issues.location: angular.tex, Lemma bulk:plane-kernels and Sec. 'Diagonal cuts and the physical reflection norm'
issues.description: The reflection-positivity and Gram-space construction is very compressed. The torus essential-loop tilt (chi vs d^k), the identification of the six-vertex Perron vacuum with the FK plane law, and the claim that the complex-phase insertions in the reflected norms are controlled by FK quantities are asserted rather than proved in checkable detail. I did not find a definite error here, but the issue above suggests that the bridge from reflected norms to positive FK costs is where the problem lies.
issues.evidence: 'Finite-volume positivity now gives the limiting Gram form.' / 'The squared norm of a lower state is then exactly the vacuum expectation ratio of its reflected configuration.'

coverage: Read in full: the introduction and main statements; observable.tex Secs 4-7 (four-change tree, marked values, residual cancellation, conditional identification, paired walls, distant normalization, factorization, gap closure, holomorphicity via reflection and extraction); exp-section definitions and budgets in preliminaries.tex (lines 510-720); angular.tex lines 1-400 and the diagonal-cut subsection. Checked numerically or symbolically: the far-branch identities d+(2-d^2)y=yG and -dy^3-(2-d^2)y^2=G; the Schwarz-Christoffel target polygon (side vectors, angles rho*pi, rho*pi, (2-3rho)*pi, rho*pi, and the exponent at infinity); crossing formula (four:crossing-formula) equals Cardy at q=1 to about 1e-9; R(u)R(-u)=(1-b^2)I; the crossing relation a(lambda-u)=b(u); a(u)e^{iu}+b(u)e^{-i(lambda-u)}=1; the budget arithmetic in hol:strict-budget. Not verified: angular Lemma bulk:boost and later in Sec 3 (spectral and Laurent-mode estimates), the current path calculus (Sec 4), the preliminaries proofs of the three logarithmic comparisons, the Jordan-quad and moving-domain transfers, the chordal identification, peeling/CLE, and the percolation-exponent section.
sibling_notes: The family 223 board had two entries. Conformal-Limits-of-Critical-Square-Lattice-Random-Cluster-Interfaces (no_gap_found, partial): it verified the four-change/Cardy formula, the tree table and the angular Laurent/sandwich, but not the holomorphicity reflection-tree bookkeeping. Self-dual-random-cluster-interfaces-below-one (rank 27, no_gap_found, partial): it did not verify 'transfer/charge budget/mixed saving'. This confirmed that the boundary-tree and Cardy computations were already checked, so I focused on the unverified holomorphicity cost budget, where I found the inconsistency. The companion papers probably share the same mixed-saving step and should be checked for the same 'stencil-independent saving' contradiction. My summary is posted to hive:oai_math:review:fam:223.
